paper_id: Security modeling and efficient computation offloading for service workflow in mobile edge computing
title: Security modeling and efficient computation offloading for service workflow in mobile edge computing
motivation: Mobile devices are resource-constrained but face complex energy-consuming applications; offloading to edge servers introduces security threats (snooping, alteration).
problem_framing: Minimize MD energy consumption under risk probability and deadline constraints, by optimally selecting security services, task locations, and execution order for workflow tasks.
key_insight: Security overhead is node-dependent and linearly/inversely proportional to secured data size, processor cores, and frequency—enabling schedulers to incorporate heterogeneous overhead into optimization.
method_signature: SEECO strategy: security overhead model + NP-hard problem formulation + GA-based coding for task order, location, and security service selection.
evaluation_criteria: Execution energy vs. risk probability (0.1-1.0), deadline constraint satisfaction, impact of security services, edge server count.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: When edge servers exceed a certain number, execution energy shows no significant reduction—indicating diminishing returns from over-provisioning.
